samples.summary: Dropping the color key (instead of storing '') lets the block's named-style color re-apply, so text-color "Reset" is a no-op inside Subtitle / Heading 3–6
samples.evidence: `resolveBlockInlines` (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:150-157) paints `{ ...namedStyleDefaults, ...inline.style }`, and the built-in named styles DO define `color` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:85,88-91: subtitle #666666, heading-3 #434343, heading-4/5/6 #666666). Before this change, the picker's Reset stored `color: ''` on the run, which is a *present* key and therefore shadowed the named-style default; `renderRun` then fell back to `theme.defaultColor` (packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:385-386, `resolveColor('')` falsy → defaultColor). After `normalizeStyleClears` the key is removed entirely, so the heading/subtitle gray is re-layered and the user sees no change when clicking Reset (same for `caretInlineStyle`'s `{ ...defaults, ...inline.style }`, packages/docs/src/model/caret-style.ts:60, so the toolbar swatch also keeps reporting the inherited color). Neither the diff nor its tests exercise a run inside a named style with an inline color default. If "Reset" is meant to mean "explicitly no color" rather than "fall back to the paragraph style", the fix belongs in the new code (e.g. keep an explicit clear marker, or have the toolbar send the resolved default) — not in layout.ts.

samples.summary: The collapsed-caret pending-style path still stores the raw `''` patch, so the toolbar/caret readers keep seeing a present-but-empty color key
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1002 does `pending.set({ ...getSelectionStyleImpl(), ...style }, cursor.position)` with the *unnormalized* patch, and `createPendingStyle.set` copies it verbatim (packages/docs/src/view/pending-style.ts:22-24). With the highlight picker's None (`onReset={() => handleColor("")}`, packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-format-group.tsx:353) fired at a collapsed caret, the pending state holds `backgroundColor: ''`, which is then merged into the values returned by `getSelectionStyle` / `getRangeStyleSummary` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2640, 2670) and into the caret-style read used for painting (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:5179). That is exactly the "a present `backgroundColor` means there is a highlight" state the new helper's doc comment says must not exist; the store write is normalized but this in-memory copy is not. Fix belongs in the new code path (normalize before `pending.set`).

samples.summary: Nothing normalizes `backgroundColor=""` / `color=""` on read, so documents already carrying the dead value (and writes from not-yet-upgraded peers) keep the #793 symptoms
samples.evidence: `parseInlineStyle` preserves the attribute verbatim (`if ('backgroundColor' in attrs) style.backgroundColor = attrs.backgroundColor;` — packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:177-178), and `MemDocStore.setDocument` / `applyInlineStyleHelper` only normalize on *write*. Any Tree node written by an older client — including a peer still running the old bundle against the same Yorkie document during rollout — keeps `backgroundColor=""`, so `normalizeInlines` still cannot merge those runs and export/`style.backgroundColor`-presence readers still see a highlight. The fix would be a read-side normalization in `parseInlineStyle` (or in `normalizeInlines`).
searchedFor: grep normalizeStyleClears call sites (block-helpers.ts, yorkie-doc-store.ts only)
grep backgroundColor across packages/docs/src (no read-side '' handling)

verdict.reason: The described mechanism is real and reachable. resolveBlockInlines layers named-style defaults under the run style (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:156), and the built-ins do define color for subtitle/heading-3..6 (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:85,88-91), so only the *presence* of a `color` key on the run suppresses that gray (paint fallback at packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:385-386). Previously the picker's Reset stored `color: ''`, which serialized verbatim into the CRDT attribute (yorkie-doc-store.ts:122) and parsed back as a present key (:177), yielding theme black. After normalizeStyleClears (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:277-286) the clear is routed to removedInlineStyleAttrs/removeStyleByPath (yorkie-doc-store.ts:145-159, 1878-1886), deleting the attribute, so the named-style gray is re-layered and Reset no longer produces black inside Subtitle/Heading 3-6 (same for the toolbar swatch via caret-style.ts:60). Two caveats refine but do not refute the finding: on the pure in-memory path (block-helpers.ts:318,348) the key stays present with value `undefined` and still shadows the default, so the visible change is limited to the CRDT/persisted path; and whether "inherit the paragraph style color" is a defect or the intended semantic is ambiguous (design doc mentions "clear formatting reverts to style" at docs/design/docs/docs-named-styles.md:43; color-picker-grid.tsx:9-11 says Reset "restore the default color" without specifying which default). That ambiguity is uncertainty, which keeps the finding rather than dropping it; the affected consumers (layout.ts, caret-style.ts) are outside the diff, squarely in this lens's lane.
